questions.subject: Use of English
questions.text:
The rise of ride-hailing applications has quietly transformed transportation in Nigerian cities over the past decade. Where commuters once haggled endlessly with bus conductors or waited indefinitely for danfo buses to fill up, many now summon a car with a few taps on a smartphone screen. The convenience is undeniable: fixed fares eliminate haggling, GPS tracking reassures anxious relatives, and cashless payment removes the need to carry loose change. Yet the revolution has not been without friction. Traditional taxi drivers have staged protests in several cities, arguing that app-based drivers operate with lower overheads and undercut established fares unfairly. Regulators, meanwhile, have struggled to keep pace, drafting rules for an industry that barely existed when most transport legislation was written. Whether ride-hailing ultimately complements or replaces traditional taxis remains an open question, but its effect on how urban Nigerians move has already proven permanent.

According to the passage, what has been one major benefit of ride-hailing apps for commuters?
options: Fixed fares that eliminate the need to haggle
questions.explanation: The passage states that fixed fares eliminate haggling as one of the conveniences of ride-hailing apps.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.text:
Few household rituals carry as much quiet significance in many Nigerian homes as the Sunday afternoon meal, prepared slowly while extended family drifts in and out of the kitchen. Unlike the rushed breakfasts of a working week, this meal is treated as an occasion, often stretching for hours as pots simmer and conversation meanders from politics to gossip to plans for the week ahead. Grandmothers guard their recipes jealously, correcting younger relatives who add too much or too little of a given spice, while children underfoot learn, almost by osmosis, the techniques that will one day be theirs to pass on. In an era of fast food and delivery apps, this ritual persists stubbornly, a reminder that some traditions resist the pull of convenience because their true value was never about efficiency in the first place.

According to the passage, how does the Sunday meal differ from weekday breakfasts?
options: It is eaten in complete silence
It is treated as an occasion and often stretches for hours
It is prepared by professional chefs only
It is always ordered from a delivery app
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly contrasts the rushed weekday breakfasts with the slow, hours-long Sunday meal treated as an occasion.

The team is playing their best today, aren't they.
The number of applicants have increased significantly.

She said I will finish the report by tomorrow.
She said that she finishes the report tomorrow.
She said that she would finish the report by the next day.

The conference which, lasted three days, attracted delegates from over twenty countries.
The conference, which lasted three days, attracted delegates from over twenty countries.

The rain continued; all night the streets were flooded by morning.
The rain continued all night the streets; were flooded by morning.

Although the weather was cold, the athletes continued training.
The weather was cold; the athletes continued training.

Because she studied hard, she passed the examination.
She studied hard, and she passed the examination with distinction.

Swimming every morning have improved her stamina.

questions.subject: Use of English

She had been studying for three hours before the exam started.

He blamed himself for the mistake.
